classification.difficultyReason: Scaffolded calculation of a face height using Pythagoras, followed by triangular face area and total surface area.

content.prompt: In the diagram opposite, $VABCD$ is a square pyramid and $O$ is the centre of square $ABCD$. If the height of the pyramid $VO=12\text{ cm}$ and $AB=10\text{ cm}$, find:

spec.description: Unshaded square pyramid with visible edges VD, VC, VB, DC and CB; hidden edges VA, AD and AB dashed. Red dashed construction segments VO, OM and VM are distinct from solid edges. O is the base centre, M is the midpoint of BC, and the right-angle marker shows VO perpendicular to OM. Ordinary source blue outlines and red hidden edges use house black.
spec.mathematics: Square ABCD has side 10 cm. V lies vertically above O with VO=12 cm. M is the midpoint of BC; OM is perpendicular to VO, and VM is the altitude of triangular face VCB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source vertex labels and construction lines are visible; no calculated lengths or areas are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the length $OM$, where $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$

answer.worked:
The distance from the centre of a square to the midpoint of a side is half its side length.
$$\begin{align*}OM&=\frac{10}{2}\\OM&=5\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

Triangle $VOM$ is right-angled at $O$. By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}VM^2&=VO^2+OM^2\\VM^2&=12^2+5^2\\VM^2&=169\\VM&=13\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

$VM$ is the perpendicular height of triangular face $VCB$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle VCB&=\frac12\times CB\times VM\\\text{Area of }\triangle VCB&=\frac12\times10\times13\\\text{Area of }\triangle VCB&=65\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: the surface area of the pyramid

answer.worked:
The four triangular faces have equal areas.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of base}&=10\times10\\\text{Area of base}&=100\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Surface area}&=4\times65+100\\\text{Surface area}&=360\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
